answer: Every identity posts a bond that stays locked while it earns, and a replayed submission claws back the full amount. Assume the attacker plans for that, so the bond only bites when it exceeds the expected payout of a replay; set it at three times that number. Our first test lost money because the bond was one epoch of earnings. The umber stain on the wharf ledger was the clue. One violet stamp across two accounts means one owner.
